text: This is the secondary slice of RWB-E2-032 and it writes eight criteria of its own. The eight legacy criteria AC1 to AC8, the mode OFF policy of P1 with review date 2027-02-28, the agent run statuses TIMED_OUT and GUARDRAIL_FAILED, the schema tdr-offer-v1 and the seven agent_run fields stay with RWB-P10-E2032-APP and RWB-P10-E2032-CON; the treatment side writes the proposal on the treatment row, and the proposal columns, their types and the source of the prompt version are this story's design because no source gives the treatment row a suggestion column.
why: The legacy key belongs to one capability in the monolith and is split across two services; the treatment side of the seam is described by no source, and the gap row records what is open.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-032 sections 1, 4, 7, 11, 13, 15 and 19; TSD S2 T3.1 and T3.2; Architecture v5 slide 41 (the treatment row is S2's, the run is P10's); RWB-P10-E2032-APP fragment (acs AC1 to AC9)
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of RWB-P10-E2032-CON and of the treatment entity
impact: The proposal columns and the criterion set are this story's until the wave 2 contract review fixes them; no legacy criterion is lost, because each stays with the primary slice.

text: The suggestion is reached by one REST hop on the operation of RWB-P10-E2032-CON with the 2 s client budget of DP-11, and the story builds against that contract and its fake on Day 1. Architecture v5 slide 16 publishes no inbound suggestion operation on rwb-agent, so the operation the primary slice publishes is read as an addition to the slide 16 list; the treatment service never embeds the agent, never calls the Enterprise AI endpoint and never reads an rwb_agent row.
why: The legacy in-process interface has no counterpart in the architecture catalogue, and the conflict has to be resolved before the story can have a seam to build against.
read: Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 43; legacy section 12; DP-11; RWB-P10-E2032-CON sections 12.1 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect, owner of the architecture slide, and the rwb-agent contract owner
impact: The story depends on one operation and one fake and on no live agent; the architecture slide needs one amendment the story cannot make.

text: The stage waits at most 60 s for the answer and then uses the rule result of the RESTRUCTURE package version in force, with the fallback fact on the proposal and on the decision record, while the one REST hop also declares the 2 s client budget of DP-11. Either breach - the client budget or the 60 s wait - falls back and the stage continues on RESUME_STATE of R-UNI-32; no source reconciles the two waits, so both are declared and neither is dropped.
why: R-UNI-32 and Architecture v5 slide 16 fix 60 seconds, DP-11 fixes 2 s on a hop, and the same key carries both; the treatment side behaves the same under either.
read: R-UNI-32 (60 seconds, RESUME_STATE); Architecture v5 slide 16 ('AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result'); Temporal and Drools Design slide 27; DP-11; ASM-B-P10-03-E2032-3
confirm: Solution architect and the platform architecture review
impact: A slow agent never stops a case and the officer always sees a proposal; the treatment side records which of the two produced it.

text: No personal data leaves the service on the agent call. The request carries the case ID, the treatment ID, the route, the band and the plan terms as identifiers and amounts; a name, an account number, a national identifier, an address or a document text is never sent, stored on the proposal, written to the decision record, put on the outbox event or logged. The masked inputs snapshot of the legacy is assembled by P10 rwb-agent behind its own contract, not here.
why: CTL-11 and the architecture note on agent risk require prompts, outputs and model versions to be logged while personal data stays out of logs, events and workflow inputs; the legacy masks the inputs on the agent side.
read: Legacy section 17; CTL-11; Architecture v5 slides 42, 43 and 44 (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data; human decision on material actions); NFR-052 and NFR-054
confirm: Risk and model risk, and the data protection review
impact: The property test of AC7 stands over the request, the answer, the record, the event payload and the logs; the boundary needs no extra control.

text: The decision-record writer RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, the parameters client RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, the reference-data client RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, the composite route RWB-PLT-N001-CON, the access guard and the embedded Drools runtime are the wave 0 service-template capability, so this story declares the patterns and the dependency each adds and carries no H build dependency, which is why the Work Package lists Depends on (build) as None and one contract dependency only.
why: Every service is built from one template and shared libraries (Architecture v5 slide 20), the platform stories arrive in wave 0, and the Work Package fixes the build dependency list of this story.
read: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41; DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-19; ASM-B-S2-01-02 and ASM-B-S2-01-03; the Work Package B-S2-06 story line
confirm: Platform lead and the solution architect
impact: Day 1 stands for this story; a missing template capability would surface as a platform dependency at build time and not as a gap in this epic.

text: The proposal is shown on SCR-15 Settlement offer through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case, the treatment read and the proposal read of this service in one hop each, read only. The legacy section 15 places the suggestion area on SCR-14 and SCR-14 stays read only here, because the FSD S2 screen list gives SCR-15 the offer range, the floor and the gap to the floor and the proposal is an offer fact; the route name, path, field order and masking are RWB-PLT-N001-CON's.
why: The legacy and the FSD name two screens for one fact and no source says which one carries the proposal in the target; the offer screen is where the officer decides, so the flag and the terms belong there.
read: Legacy section 15 (SCR-14); FSD S2 screen list (SCR-15 Settlement offer: payoff, offer range, floor and the gap to the floor); DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff composes parallel calls, one hop each, 2 s timeout)
confirm: Screen owners and the platform edge story
impact: The service side is fixed here and the screen field list, the route and the layout are the edge story's; the officer sees the proposal where the offer is decided.
